NFL placekicking · 1938–2026 league totals · 61,785 kicks play-by-play since 1999

Field Goal Drift

Kickers are attempting longer field goals and converting more of them. The question this page tests is whether that holds after accounting for the distance mix, venue and weather, and where the rule changes sit against the trend.

The long view

League regular-season totals from Pro-Football-Reference, back to the first season it records attempts. Distance bands exist from 1960 and are complete from about 1970, so the range metrics start there. Gold lines mark rule changes that bear on kicking. These series ignore the filters.

Efficiency, adjusted for distance

Raw make rate rises partly because coaches can choose easier kicks, so this compares each season's actual make rate with the rate a 1999–2026 pooled kicker would have achieved on that season's exact set of distances. The gap is makes over expected. A season that kicks longer and still beats expectation is the strongest evidence for better kicking.

Expected rate uses a logistic curve in distance fitted to all 28,021 field goal attempts 1999–2026 (no season terms), so the zero line is the 28-year pooled average kicker. Filters apply.

Range

Distance of attempts and makes by season. A rising 90th percentile with a flat mean would say only the tail is moving; both rising says coaches trust the leg across the board.

Make % by distance band

Points with fewer than 8 attempts are hidden; hover for counts.

Season × distance make rate

Darker is higher make %. Hatched cells have fewer than 10 attempts.

Controlled model

A logistic regression on every field goal attempt 1999–2026 with a cubic distance curve, a separate intercept and distance slope for each season, and terms for venue, temperature, wind, reported precipitation and playoffs. The lines show the modeled probability of a make from 40, 50 and 55 yards in mild, calm, dry outdoor conditions, with 95% intervals. This panel uses all data and ignores the filters.

Condition effects (odds ratio vs mild, calm, dry outdoor)

An odds ratio of 0.75 at a baseline make probability of 80% is about a 5-point drop; at 60% it is about a 7-point drop.

Venue and weather

Within the selected seasons, make rate and makes over expected by condition. Weather comes from the pregame report for the game, so it describes the day rather than the moment of the kick, and retractable roofs open or closed are taken from the game record.

Share of field goal attempts by venue type. The indoor share moves with stadium construction and team relocation, so it is a composition effect the expected-rate comparison does not remove.

Extra points

The 2015 move of the PAT snap to the 15-yard line turned every extra point into a 33-yard kick, which makes it a fixed-distance accuracy test across the last eleven seasons. Filters apply.

Data and method

Kick-level data. nflverse play-by-play, seasons 1999 to 2026 week 5 (28 files, field-goal and extra-point plays only). Venue comes from the roof field (dome, closed, open, outdoors). Temperature and wind come from the structured fields where present and are otherwise parsed from the pregame weather string. Precipitation is classified from the weather description: a clause that names rain, showers, drizzle, snow, flurries or sleet without a hedge such as “chance” or “possible” counts as reported precipitation, hedged clauses count as possible, and 1999–2000 games, which have no description, are unknown.

League totals. Pro-Football-Reference league kicking totals. Totals for 1996–2026 are exact; earlier seasons are per-team averages multiplied by the team count, so attempt counts are rounded but rates are unaffected. These are NFL-only (no AFL before 1970) and regular season only. 2026 is partial.

Rule changes. From the 1974 and 1994 NFL season records, NFL competition-committee summaries, and reporting on kicking-ball rules (1999, 2007, 2025). The 2026 rule changes concern kickoffs and onside kicks and none touch field goals.

Sources: nflverse play-by-play · Pro-Football-Reference league kicking · 1974 NFL season · 1994 NFL season · AP via Fox Sports on K-balls · Football Zebras on 2026 rules
